android.desc:
Sky Map helps you identify stars, planets, nebulae, and constellations in real-time. Originally developed as Google Sky Map, it is now open source.

Find us online:

⭐ Official Website: stardroid.app ⭐ Open Source: Contribute on GitHub ⭐ Join the Community:     • Facebook @stardroidapp     • X @skymapdevs

App permissions:

Sky Map has no required permissions. Each permission below is optional — you may refuse any of them and still use the app. Nothing is requested at startup; each is asked for only when you first use the feature that needs it, and each can be withdrawn separately in your device settings. ⭐ Location (optional) — used to draw the sky for where you are. Refuse it and you can enter a place name or coordinates by hand instead. Your location never leaves your device. ⭐ Camera (optional) — used only by through-camera mode, which overlays the sky on the live camera view. Refuse it and every other mode works as normal. The image is never recorded or transmitted. ⭐ Notifications (optional) — used only to tell you about meteor-shower peaks and tonight's sky, if you ask for them. They stay off until you turn them on.

It surprises me how many Android users don't know about this great free Google app...

https://market.android.com/details?id=com.google.android.stardroid

It's not quite the same thing, but on Android you can use Sky Map [1] and search for "M6". (The actual center is just off from the star in Sagittarius that is closest to M6 (γ2 Sagittarii), but I don't believe Sky Map will let you search for it directly.)

[1] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.stardroid
